title: Atrophic Gastritis
subject: Pathology
summary: Atrophic gastritis is chronic inflammation with gland loss, leading to hypochlorhydria and intestinal metaplasia. In East Africa, H. pylori and autoimmune causes dominate, with significant risk of gastric cancer.

sections.p: Atrophic gastritis is the loss of gastric glands and mucosal atrophy, usually seen on biopsy. It is diagnosed by histology showing gland loss, intestinal metaplasia, or by endoscopic appearance of pale, atrophic mucosa.

t.b: Shows pale, atrophic mucosa; biopsies confirm gland loss and metaplasia.
Identifies gland loss, intestinal metaplasia, and inflammation.
A low ratio (<3) suggests atrophic gastritis of the corpus.
Positive indicates H. pylori infection, a common cause.

sections.p: The OLGA (Operative Link on Gastritis Assessment) system stages atrophic gastritis from 0 to IV based on extent and severity of atrophy, guiding cancer risk.
b: OLGA I – mild, limited to antrum
OLGA II – moderate, antrum and body

sections.p: In low‑resource settings, H. pylori infection is the leading cause. Autoimmune disease is second, followed by long‑term PPI use and nutritional deficiencies.
b: H. pylori infection – chronic gastritis leading to atrophy

sections.p: Patients may be asymptomatic or have vague epigastric discomfort, early satiety, nausea, or anemia. In advanced cases, weight loss and bleeding may occur.
Choose tests that are available locally and interpret them with awareness of limitations.

t.b: Detects atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, and excludes malignancy.
Low ratio indicates corpus atrophy; useful where endoscopy is scarce.
Positive suggests infection; treat if confirmed.
Shows anaemia; low reticulocytes suggest chronic disease.
Low B12 indicates pernicious gastritis; low folate suggests nutritional deficiency.
Detects hidden bleeding; positive in advanced disease.

sections.p: Complications include gastric cancer, B12 deficiency anaemia, and severe bleeding. Red flags warrant urgent referral.
Treat the underlying cause, provide nutritional support, and monitor for progression.
b: Eradicate H. pylori with triple therapy (clarithromycin, amoxicillin, PPI) – avoid if resistance suspected

t.b: Reduces acid, allowing mucosal healing; avoid long‑term use unless necessary.
Treat pernicious anaemia and prevent neurological sequelae.
Ensure adequate protein, iron, B12, and folate intake.

sections.p: Regular surveillance endoscopy for high OLGA stages; repeat H. pylori testing after treatment; maintain adequate nutrition.
b: Endoscopy every 3–5 years if OLGA III/IV
Vaccinate against hepatitis B to reduce gastric inflammation risk

faq.q: How do I differentiate atrophic gastritis from H. pylori gastritis?
faq.a: Atrophic gastritis shows gland loss and intestinal metaplasia on biopsy; H. pylori gastritis shows active inflammation but preserved glands.

faq.q: Why is B12 deficiency common in atrophic gastritis?
faq.a: Loss of parietal cells reduces intrinsic factor, impairing B12 absorption.

faq.q: Can long‑term PPI use cause atrophic gastritis?
faq.a: Yes, chronic acid suppression can lead to hypochlorhydria and gland loss over time.

exam: A 45‑year‑old man with chronic epigastric pain and iron deficiency anaemia – what is the first investigation? — Endoscopy with biopsy to look for atrophy and H. pylori.
A patient on long‑term PPI develops B12 deficiency – what is the likely mechanism? — Loss of intrinsic factor due to parietal cell atrophy.
A 60‑year‑old woman with weight loss and dysphagia – what red flag warrants urgent referral? — New onset dysphagia suggests possible gastric cancer.
You find intestinal metaplasia on biopsy – what is the next step in surveillance? — Endoscopy every 3–5 years if OLGA III/IV.
A patient with positive anti‑parietal cell antibodies – what treatment is indicated? — Vitamin B12 injections.
You have limited access to endoscopy – which surrogate test can estimate corpus atrophy? — Serum pepsinogen I/II ratio.
You suspect H. pylori but cannot perform urea breath test – what alternative test? — Anti‑H. pylori IgG serology.
